svg.title: Type I and type II errors in hypothesis testing, two-dimensional version (unlabelled)
svg.desc: Two-dimensional diagram of a statistical hypothesis test. A horizontal axis shows values t of the test statistic T, and a vertical axis shows the density of T. Two bell-shaped normal density curves with the same spread are drawn: the density of T under the null hypothesis H0 in blue on the left, and the density of T under the alternative hypothesis H1 in dark red on the right. A vertical line at the critical value c, marked as a point on the t axis, separates the acceptance region to the left, shown as a green band below the axis, from the critical region to the right, shown as an orange band. The figure has no text labels. The shaded, hatched blue tail of the H0 curve right of c represents alpha, the probability of a type I error. The shaded, cross-hatched magenta tail of the H1 curve left of c represents beta, the probability of a type II error. Two-dimensional companion to a figure adapted from "PPV, NPV, Sensitivity and Specificity" by Luigi Albert Maria, Wikimedia Commons, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.
